Dark, aged alcoholic drinks—especially **brandy, whiskey, bourbon, dark rum, and red wine** —generally cause the worst hangovers. They contain higher levels of **congeners** (byproducts of fermentation and aging) that can intensify next-day symptoms compared to clear spirits like vodka or gin at the same amount of alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXHX5vGDdwPHufHmiie5UodXhJz35UQMSjcFCXgX16_6PSPRhLpaRedur8gnnvgY-iXNhL3FfKjsupAC1TDTd_yBR1yUxDYIt5b639Uef8Cdp9sPdRzUo7krcwYbLjzRr5Zh9m0tEO)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1yqT4EglH6OG9nwi1ILzxmlBXNIq_K2omrcG5_WMEr1_b0h4w74qcZRVzVds7F6PXYZslM6mumSf4QIdbWxIiBRzbttHO7DP7zDqf-fkwXAvqIF5oTrN3WokqewUKbAc40bHfJNOf3dKo-oB2gNDY5M-vPm9JrCXPFh_bvVlCA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjgEBxCJF12pL2avu9bmZFTrT_IR9jFjuiZMkIpRnq428e5rnME2g0lkrq5mcJvQJYRx99ICJXKncCO1y_WfFbaw4iaYzpY-xRHoNIT-NfAUVGKOJF4LxZyncOp4DJ0_ztBHyte5vSgWBJE0W4T9qa3_ilTA0ibg3YDtmadTLOSyc5GBz51_LRtA0WZ7ygz_u)

### Worst Offenders and Why

- **Brandy and cognac:** Often rank at the top for congener levels (such as methanol), which can worsen headaches and nausea.
- **Whiskey and bourbon:** Aged in wood barrels, giving them heavy congener loads that slow recovery.
- **Dark rum:** Contains higher levels of congeners (like propanol) than light rum.
- **Red wine:** Combines congeners with tannins and sulfites, which trigger headaches for many people.
- **Sugary or carbonated drinks:** Sweet cocktails and sparkling wines can lead to drinking faster or consuming more without realizing it, while carbonation speeds alcohol absorption.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1x4yjEO-ySX1r_Ua9HAoHNe7_rnR_NdY8tiJ-isjrHRzEUC6RkRKWhYN62OMHGW4JUxnGKRHYxPYoafTbJ3hmgb3XwxKtqxm0X9Zlk9XdRMTVVnb1pOcIchCP_nc9vDlO2NOgr4SAVYUYckXZt4D55JP7-nulo8rmsAJLrae3DW_oW_I3tgEs_eUaXUEbMvlxugE)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShgEBxCJF18skObY9itt3nzo1KVTbmFusdRXF6mBhZCtWx4gz0AZRfZms2xRZVgYbEuzFM4VFHqEbF_OWhY5pSS4qO6zz98CZnNCDvHUJTU4z_ZamblUBxihW9mtUzjANHpFKvQa994Jck6uaoGolWmA9GeZ7D73K9wqwhhrcj9Vs9_7UCj6EQA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjgEBxCJF12pL2avu9bmZFTrT_IR9jFjuiZMkIpRnq428e5rnME2g0lkrq5mcJvQJYRx99ICJXKncCO1y_WfFbaw4iaYzpY-xRHoNIT-NfAUVGKOJF4LxZyncOp4DJ0_ztBHyte5vSgWBJE0W4T9qa3_ilTA0ibg3YDtmadTLOSyc5GBz51_LRtA0WZ7ygz_u)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXaxF622VOV6j7Rel-MbZX89mdPnIzBL338fUzqcT7zR1Z-j3UrduVtSFRH637E8KrPemWsSNCKZpWWcKmqFvnwglrYiZirkHpvUSf1Pv7BNuEpOCRqqA-sC3olbpZF-q1)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1yqT4EglH6OG9nwi1ILzxmlBXNIq_K2omrcG5_WMEr1_b0h4w74qcZRVzVds7F6PXYZslM6mumSf4QIdbWxIiBRzbttHO7DP7zDqf-fkwXAvqIF5oTrN3WokqewUKbAc40bHfJNOf3dKo-oB2gNDY5M-vPm9JrCXPFh_bvVlCA)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXHX5vGDdwPHufHmiie5UodXhJz35UQMSjcFCXgX16_6PSPRhLpaRedur8gnnvgY-iXNhL3FfKjsupAC1TDTd_yBR1yUxDYIt5b639Uef8Cdp9sPdRzUo7krcwYbLjzRr5Zh9m0tEO)[[7]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXXnAvDxhV9tC3ax493Q7Y63L7rdfn5wLsLlglyqDzA46vQm3m2BW3wB2-KOiT7ipZgtEplcttE5c8nXiGx80WrpVkJpLHvKrzyGIkEEOqM-2yM-WIoacOj9maUAxgd4IgnViNgHdOvORiib-e2-MQbZ0)[[8]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1w37totR6QHIx97VLMPBGgNmhH9ntheY4AVZsCrjh95A6YlVEwDu5rvitbYZS3xD1YvtRfKOoCemDX5wbHVItgMPqI7mJ7vSALQLoFUPlsetRFG10YNrTD_RGVaeD9wGcmJXSIzUaP5RJcCdAs_Bl5StUcYH18qqQJs892J7KQ)[[9]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXheYoGp9_SPoU0YdehKi1mc19XLrYABnTrDvZEEj9r1PdUN883bCwUE6a-hdv4hMocbx6dA2uXGxEAST-QlawQLYRE956BSBccIEGTyz4ykUybNXICtkfneXQctMUN6Ef)

### What Matters Most
While drink choice plays a role, **how much alcohol you drink** and **how fast you drink it** remain the biggest drivers of a hangover. Dehydration, poor sleep, and drinking on an empty stomach also make mornings worse regardless of the type of alcohol.
